decision.title: The stylesheet reader and static expressions (packet )

body.p: , after , , , . src/xslt_ast.c (the builder of ), src/xslt_read.c with src/xslt_read_internal.h (sxml_xslt_read_stylesheet), src/xslt_static.c with src/xslt_static_internal.h (the static scope); the packet named no headers, so each module has its own.

item.p: Walk: each module is parsed by the XML parser into an arena tree with locations; one explicit stack of open elements () holds the elements of every module being read, so an include or import pushes the new module's document frame and is read in place ('s pre-order). Text runs are collected between elements (comments, PIs, xsl:note dropped, 3.11.1) and stripped by 3.11.1's rules.

Tables: one row per XSLT element, generated from the 4.0 schema (attributes and their types, ) and the element syntax summaries of the spec (required attributes, category, content model); one row per attribute (value syntax, keyword mask). Where the two disagree the schema wins (record-type has no constructor, field has default).

Static expressions (9.7) run through the one front end, lowering and evaluator (sxml_xpath_lower, sxml_evaluator_evaluate) with a static scope: the static variables so far (later hides earlier) and a function table that puts system-property, available-system-properties, function-available, element-available and type-available (native rows of a small function library) in front of the processor's. 4.10 may move these rows to a library part for non-static XSLT expressions. Shadow attributes are value templates evaluated to a string (the AST is that of a string template, ); the shadow's static context is the element's native or fixed namespaces with the parent's default element namespace and base URI. Values of static variables are coerced by binding them to a declared variable (XTTE0570, XTTE0590 for supplied parameters); a required static parameter without value is XTDE0050.

Modules (3.10): hrefs are resolved against the element's static base URI and asked from the resolver as XSLT_MODULE; unavailable or not well-formed is XTSE0165. A reference to a module whose URI is on the path being read is ignored when every step of that path and the reference is an include (an include cycle, 4.0), else XTSE0210; an include of a URI already in the stylesheet level is ignored (included_module 0).

Node contents (TEXT_NODE value templates, xsl:select) name their expression before it exists: the AST numbers expressions in order, so the reader gives the next index and hands the AST over after the node. sxml_xslt_ast_add_node marks a module simplified when its first node is a synthesized STYLESHEET (the header has no other writer for the flag).

Checks while reading: XTSE0010 (placement, order, required attributes and children), XTSE0090, XTSE0805, XTSE0020 (values), XTSE0110, XTSE0120, XTSE0125, XTSE0130, XTSE0260, XTSE0280, XTSE0340/0350/0370 and XPST0003 from the front ends, XTSE0500, XTSE0530, XTSE0740, XTSE0808, XTSE0812, XTSE1430, XTSE0122 (fixed-namespaces by URI is not read), XTSE1660 (import-schema, strict/lax validation, schema types; ). Errors keep their code and point at the attribute or element (module URI, line, column; an expression's own offset added on its first line).

Left to lowering: duplicate declarations, XTSE3450 between static variables, the arity and ordering rules beyond leading children, the values static variables give non-static expressions (the AST does not keep them: lowering re-evaluates their select with the same scope).
